steps.text: Bring water and sugar to a boil in a medium saucepan until sugar dissolves. Reduce heat and stir in cranberries, pureed orange, apple, pear, dried fruit, pecans, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cranberries burst. Remove from heat, and let cool to room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry Sauce Extraordinaire
raw_recipe.description: The best cranberry sauce recipe combines fresh cranberries, orange, apple, pear, dried fruit, pecans, and spices to make a classic holiday side dish.
raw_recipe.name: Cranberry Sauce Extraordinaire

recipeInstructions.text: Bring water and sugar to a boil in a medium saucepan until sugar dissolves. Reduce heat and stir in cranberries, pureed orange, apple, pear, dried fruit, pecans, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cranberries burst. Remove from heat, and let cool to room temperature.

review.reviewBody: Literally the BEST cranberry sauce EVER. You will never again buy the canned kind. I followed the recipe to a T, except that I substituted one small can of mandarine orange slices instead of one orange. It made prep super easy. For the dried fruit, I used the Sunmaid bits of fruit that include raisins, prunes, cherries and apricots. Everyone at our Thanksgiving dinner loved this sauce. My mother asked for seconds and thirds! The recipe makes a TON, but it lasts in the fridge and only gets better as the flavors blend. I found myself craving it by the spoonful the days following Thanksgiving, so I would heat a few spoonfulls in the microwave until it was warm and ate it right out of the bowl. I am still eating it with cream cheese on bagels for breakfast every morning! This one will be a staple at my holiday table every year! The best way to describe it is that it tastes like "fall." The yummy fall spices make this dish.

Doesn't look like the picture at all....just fyi. I liked the recipe, it was more like a fruity dessert than a cranberry sauce, which was actually nice since some people don't like Cranberry sauce. I would recommend that you half the sugar, cook the cranberries in a different pot, put the remaining pot of fruit in a food processor after cooked and then add the cranberries after processing. This would give it more of a "cranberry dish" feel. It is very tasty, but make sure to half the sugar....the fruit was more than enough sweet.

Part 2 of 2 Parts!! [CHEF'S NOTE: The second time, on my commercial range, I chose not to simmer, but to use a low boil instead once the syrup was ready. The cranberries began to burst almost as soon as they were immersed, and my doubled recipe was cooked in about 15 minutes, contributing to the apples and pears retaining their consistency. I recommend the higher heat instead of the longer simmer.] A double recipe yields a little more than 3 quarts. And I can tell you it won't be enough! The finished product is very jam-like in texture, and reducing the sugar helps to not overwhelm the tartness of the cranberries. You will not want to pass on this recipe. It is a genuine crowd pleaser! You may find that doubling again (to 4x) will provide the leftovers you'll be sorry you didn't have more of. We have used this on toast and even as an ice cream topping!! (Try it, you'll love it.) It will make an excellent gift when packed in 1/2 pint mason jars using a standard jam hot-pack method. Just tell the recipients to use it as soon as possible so they can ask you for the recipe before all the cranberries are gone from the market until next year.

As a professional chef, I knew this was a winning recipe when I saw it "on screen". You will NOT be disappointed by this recipe which is easy enough for your child to do with supervision. I made this for the first time -- twice in the same week. First in a crockpot overnight, then on the stovetop. Both times doubling the recipe and omitting the nuts and salt (no reason for salt in this recipe at all). Also reduced the sugar to 1-3/4 cups instead of 2 cups. Used smaller-sized navel oranges pureed to juice and pulp in a food processor, and golden raisins, mediterranean apricots, mango slices, and dark cherries as the dried fruit (all but the raisins chopped in the food processor with steel knife blade), and Granny Smith apples and Bosc pears cut by hand. In a 6-quart crockpot overnight, the apples and pears broke down and became indistinguishable in the sauce. And the lower heat of the crockpot means having to "help" the cranberries to burst.

This is really exceptional! I made a double batch of this. I took the advice of another reviewer and added dried cranberries instead of other dried fruit as I wanted a true cranberry taste. It turned out a nice deep red. We have some diabetics in the family so I only used 2/3 cup of Splenda in place of sugar for the double batch and it was nice and tangy! I made a mistake though and as odd as it sounds, it worked out for the best! Even though I had doubled the recipe, I accidentally only added one cup of water! It turned out nice and thick (not runny) but watch the temp if you do that so it doesn't burn. Got rave reviews and requests for the recipe which is the greatest compliment! Going to make more for Christmas next week! I only rated four stars since I used the Splenda and only 1/2 the water for the double recipe, otherwise I would have rated it five stars! **Edited** to add that the second time I made this, I used around 3/4 cup of Splenda, great taste but think everyone prefers it made with 2/3 cup of Splenda, more tang to the taste with 2/3 cup.

This is addictive and so easy to make. You will be scraping the bottom of your cooking dish. I followed directions with a few changes. 

Threw all ingredients in the slow cooker & cooked on low for five hours. Do leave in for full five hours as it takes a long time for nutmeg flavor to diffuse - tried the sauce half way through and did not like strong nutmeg flavor, however at the end of five hours it was imperceptible.

1) Instead of cup of water: 1/4 cup #Cheribundi Tart cherry juice (cold) + 3/4 c boiling water. I think any fruit juice would work.
2) 1/2 cup of sugar instead of a cup as recommended by others. Dissolved the sugar in the hot liquid before adding to slow cooker. 
3) Used dried Cherry Fruit Medley bits from a local produce store which included equal amounts of chopped cherries, peaches, pears, golden raisins, apricots
4) For my pear, used a ripe Bosc

I didn't have a pear. Used dried cherries, blueberries and raisins. I used the whole orange including the peel . Put all fruit except cranberries in the Vitamix for a few pulses and then added to cranberries. This is much better and more interesting than plain cranberry sauce.

As some reviewers suggested, I halved the sugar. By doing this though, I found it too tart for me (even with the sweet fruits) so I did add the full amount later. When dissolving it, I used half water and half orange juice. I also used a can of drained mandarin oranges to make it easier, coarsely chopping so they wouldn't be in whole pieces. For fruits, I used dried cherries, cranberries and apricots. I'd chop my pecans a little finer the next time; I would prefer that over the larger pieces I had. I also added about a tblsp of brandy to the mixture. It's cooling now but will be great for Thanksgiving this week, and I'm thinking even to gift for Christmas. Nice recipe!

I'm rating the "idea" of this recipe. I had to work with what I had which was - 1/2 a 12 oz bag of fresh crans, 1 can of whole cran sauce. I sm can of mandarin oranges & sm can of pears. I drained the mandarin juice into the fresh cranberries (with a splash of water) and added my peeled diced apple. Used fresh grated nutmeg & cinammon. After that cooked I pureed with a stick blender. I cut the mandarin oranges in half, diced up the drained canned pears and added that along with more cinnamon and a tsp of fresh ginger and ground coriander. Added the can of whole cranberries. Mixed all that up on the stovetop and let it simmer for 10 minutes. I think using the juice from mandarin oranges along with the canned pears & the apple; gave it plenty sweet. Oh...I added 1/4 C of golden raisins during initial cooking before pureed. No other dried fruit was used in my rendition. Anyway, was a great starting point that you can toy with. Love the spices in it! I found it tasted even better sitting it the fridge overnight. I gotta try this on some cream cheese with a bagel, that sounds really good.

I just made this and it is fantastic. I did decrease the sugar to 3/4 cup and used 1/2 cup water and 1/2 cup apple cider for the liquid. I used dried cherries and apricots as my dried fruits, and added a cinnamon stick to the mixture as it was cooking. I will definitely be making this for Thanksgiving. A nice change from classic cranberry sauce.

I've made this a number of times now, and I've finally settled on "my version". I use about 1/4 c of sugar instead of a full cup, use a small can of mandarin oranges in place of the fresh orange, add a small can of crushed pineapple, and if I can't find good pears, I use 2 apples instead. Once everything has cooked and completely cooled, and I add a pint of fresh blueberries. I try to cook at least the day before to give all the flavors time to meld, but I don't add the pecans until just before serving so they don't get mushy. Terrific recipe as is - all of my little modifications are just personal preferences.
The orange didn't break down while cooking. I even used a hand blended. Maybe a little more sugar??

SOOOOOOOOO DELICIOUS!!! I love Nicole’s “EXTRAORDINARE” version. And…….she is absolutely correct. I wanted to eat the entire bowl just to eat it. I used fresh cranberries b/c every store was out of frozen. Exact same process….SUPER EASY.
Delicious!! Doesn’t compare to the one you get at the store!!!
Fantastic. Everyone loved it!

For my dried mix, I used a little pineapple chunks, small amount of dried cherries and mango slices. I would love to try it with dried peaches next time. This was simply phenomenal. I did run it through a food mill at the end of cooking and then scoop the bits back into the smooth sauce. I omitted the pecans. Thank you for sharing a fabulous recipe! That is so customizable and delicious.
My whole family LOVED THIS! It will our new annual FAV!!

I have been making this for the last 10 years..! It's a family favorite for sure. I definitely half the sugar, not necesarry with all the other fruit in the recipe...! The best EVER cranberry - must try, you won't be disappointed - honest!
It was way too sweet for me.

I never leave reviews, but this is THE BEST cranberry sauce and everyone loves it. I do not add quite that much sugar, it doesn't need it in my opinion, but I don't love a lot of sugar. The dried fruit and regular fruit has plenty. I usually only add half a cup or a little more to taste. My daughter gets sooo excited every year for it. Thank you so much for sharing!!
